themes.label: Bots and AI misinformation lack free-speech rights
themes.definition: Artificially generated misinformation and programmed bots spreading hate and lies are argued not to be protected by freedom of expression, which belongs to humans.
themes.inclusion: Include passages on AI-generated misinformation, bots, propaganda or information integrity.
themes.exclusion: Exclude general human rights references to AI without information/speech content.
themes.boundary_cases: Arguments about rights applying only to humans also touch AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS, but the disinformation focus is primary.

examples.quote: Freedom of expression is for human beings — not for programmed bots that spread hate, lies and fear
State-sponsored propaganda or artificially generated misinformation that is intended to sow discord and disunity

themes.label: Multilateral cooperation against destructive AI
themes.definition: AI raises serious questions demanding close multilateral cooperation to prevent it becoming a tool of destruction.
themes.inclusion: Include calls for multilateral cooperation to manage AI risks.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages on AI benefits only.
themes.boundary_cases: 'Destruction rather than creation' framing may also be read as AI_OPPORTUNITY_RISK_DUALITY.

examples.quote: will demand close multilateral cooperation to avoid the very real risk of this technology becoming a tool of destruction rather than creation

value.rationale: A single Icelandic passage calling for multilateral cooperation on AI's destructive risk and focusing specifically on AI-generated misinformation and bots, arguing free-speech rights belong only to humans.
